item.title: NZ Q3 Unemployment rate 5.7% (expected 5.5%, prior 5.6%)
item.description:
The miss on every major measure is likely to weigh on the New Zealand dollar and trim pricing for a December rate hike. The kiwi was already near a cycle low against the Australian dollar after last week’s RBNZ hold, and the gap with a more hawkish RBA now looks set to widen. The weak jobs figures argue against tightening, but the RBNZ’s hawks have focused on core inflation and fuel costs. A labour market miss alone may not settle the debate, so inflation expectations surveys later this month carry extra weight. Front-end swap rates are the market to watch for how far hike bets are pared.

--- Banks called the peak in New Zealand unemployment, but the labour market went the other way, and the RBNZ’s December hike now looks a harder sell.

Summary:

  • Unemployment rose to 5.7% in Q3 from 5.6%, against a Reuters poll forecast of 5.5%
  • Employment fell 0.1% on the quarter, against expectations of a 0.4% gain, and Q2 growth was revised down to 0.3%
  • The participation rate dropped to 70.4% from 70.6%, below the 70.7% forecast
  • Private sector wages excluding overtime rose 0.4% on the quarter and 2.0% on the year, both slightly below forecasts
  • The RBNZ held rates at 2.75% last week on a 4:3 vote, with the next decision on 9 December
  • New Zealand holds a general election on Saturday

New Zealand’s unemployment rate rose to 5.7% in the third quarter, above expectations of 5.5%, as employment unexpectedly fell and wage growth slowed, data from Statistics New Zealand showed on Wednesday.

Employment declined 0.1% from the previous quarter, against a Reuters poll forecast of a 0.4% gain. The participation rate dropped to 70.4% from 70.6%, below the 70.7% expected. Unemployment rose even though fewer people were looking for work, which points to weak hiring rather than a growing labour force. Earlier figures were also revised lower, with second-quarter employment growth cut to 0.3% from 0.5%.

The result runs against bank forecasts that had pointed to a peak in joblessness. Westpac had expected the rate to ease to 5.5%, while ANZ had forecast no change at 5.6%. The June quarter reading of 5.6% was already the highest since 2015.

Wage pressures also eased. Private sector wages excluding overtime rose 0.4% in the quarter, below the 0.5% expected, taking annual growth to 2.0% from 2.1%.

The data lands at a sensitive moment for the Reserve Bank of New Zealand. On 28 October it held the official cash rate at 2.75% in a 4:3 vote, surprising markets that had largely priced a hike. The majority cited weaker than expected inflation, stable inflation expectations and subdued wage growth, and argued that two earlier rate increases needed time to work. Wednesday’s figures support that case on both jobs and pay.

Westpac had described today’s release as the first key input before the RBNZ’s next decision on 9 December, while still forecasting a hike at that meeting. The bank cautioned that the move was not a done deal, and a weaker labour market makes that case harder to argue.

New Zealand holds a general election on Saturday, adding further uncertainty to the policy outlook ahead of the December meeting. 

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: Nasdaq rebounds as chip stocks rally and Dow slips
item.description:
U.S. stocks closed mixed on Tuesday. The Nasdaq Composite led the rebound with a 0.83% gain, and the Nasdaq 100 added 0.68%. The S&P 500 and Russell 2000 also finished higher, while the Dow fell 197 points. Chip stocks helped lead the move, with Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom all gaining more than 2%.

The S&P 500’s close told only part of the story. Decliners outnumbered advancers 318 to 167 in the index, and only nine of the Dow’s 30 stocks finished higher. Nasdaq breadth was positive, with 1,630 advancers against 1,566 decliners. Buyers made more progress in tech, but participation was still fairly narrow.

U.S. closing levels

  • Dow Industrial Average −197.00 points (−0.38%) to 51,792.19
  • S&P 500 +27.52 points (+0.36%) to 7,568.92
  • Nasdaq Composite +207.69 points (+0.83%) to 25,372.01
  • Russell 2000 +6.57 points (+0.23%) to 2,812.45
  • Nasdaq 100 +190.44 points (+0.68%) to 28,180.26

Chip stocks lead, while Apple bucks the move

  • Microsoft rose 2.74%, Meta gained 2.36%, Nvidia added 2.27% and Amazon rose 2.06%. Alphabet edged up 0.37%, while Apple fell 1.90%.
  • Credo gained 7.78%, Monolithic Power Systems rose 6.78% and SanDisk added 4.78%. AMD closed up 3.65% at $483.90 heading into its earnings release, while Texas Instruments rose 3.46% and Broadcom gained 3.07%.
  • Outside the chip names, Bloom Energy rose 9.05%, AppLovin gained 7.28%, Nebius added 7.25% and GE Vernova climbed 6.49%.

Nasdaq buyers keep the 200-day moving averages in play

The Nasdaq Composite closed at 25,372.01 after Monday’s selloff took it to 25,145.95, just above its rising 200-day moving average near 25,073. The buyers have some room off that support now. On a pullback, Monday’s low is the first barometer. A move below it would put the 200-day back in focus, and getting and staying below the average would increase the bearish bias.

The Nasdaq 100 came even closer to its 200-day moving average on Monday, bottoming at 27,967.44 against the average near 27,952.83. Tuesday’s close at 28,180.26 gives buyers some breathing room. The next test on the topside is near 28,538. Getting and staying above that level would have traders looking toward the 28,822–28,953 swing area.

Trading lesson

Pair the index close with the advance-decline count. In a capitalization-weighted index like the S&P 500, gains in a few large stocks can lift the index even as most members fall. If the index extends its rebound and more stocks join in, that tells you buyers are gaining ground across more of the market. Tuesday’s S&P 500 close leaves that as a question for the next session.

After the close, AMD and Super Micro beat on earnings and revenue

All seven companies topped adjusted EPS estimates, and six beat on revenue. Super Micro Computer posted the largest revenue beat of the group, coming in $3.88 billion above expectations. AMD beat by $0.14 per share and $300 million in revenue. Booking Holdings was the lone revenue miss, coming in $650 million below expectations even as earnings beat.

  • AMD — Adj. EPS $2.09 vs. $1.95 (BEAT) · Revenue $13.40B vs. $13.10B (BEAT). Shares are trading at $524 up 8.32%. It's 100 day moving averages at $529.15. Stay above is more bullish.

  • Block — Adj. EPS $1.13 vs. $1.03 (BEAT) · Revenue $6.72B vs. $6.58B (BEAT). Shares are trading at $82.10 up 8.03%. The price is back above its 100 day moving average at $78.24

  • Arista Networks — Adj. EPS $1.20 vs. $1.08 (BEAT) · Revenue $3.66B vs. $3.33B (BEAT). Shares are trading at $182.25 up 7.26%. Its 100 day moving averages at $186.18.

  • Super Micro Computer — Adj. EPS $1.81 vs. $1.20 (BEAT) · Revenue $19.90B vs. $16.02B (BEAT). It's shares are trading at $33.69 up 7.29%. Its 100 day moving averages at $34.28.

  • Booking Holdings — Adj. EPS $4.66 vs. $4.49 (BEAT) · Revenue $8.90B vs. $9.55B (MISS). It's shares are trading down 2.26% at $152.82. The price is moving away from its 100 hour moving average at $156.60, and its 200 hour moving average at $158.17.

  • Amgen — Adj. EPS $6.45 vs. $5.79 (BEAT) · Revenue $10.40B vs. $10.07B (BEAT) · Adj. operating income $4.70B vs. $4.33B (BEAT). Shares are trading at $449 is down -2.66%. The next key target on the downside is the 100 hour moving average at $446.93.

item.title: Economic and event calendar in Asia Wednesday, November 4, 2026 - NZ jobs report, China PMI
item.description:
The RatingDog PMI data follows official and their manufacturing PMIs earlier this week:

  • details on these in the wrap for Monday, investingLive Asia-Pacific market news: Oil eases on Doha talks

The NZ Q3 labour market data is due at 10:45am New Zealand time. 

What’s expected

Forecasts range from 5.4% to 5.6%. The June quarter’s 5.6% was the highest since September 2015. Westpac expects employment to rise 0.5% and the rate to slip to 5.5%. ANZ expects employment up 0.3% and the rate unchanged at 5.6%. ANZ’s flat call rests on a rise in labour force participation absorbing the job gains. The RBNZ’s September forecast was 5.5%. Wage growth is expected to stay modest. Private-sector labour cost growth is forecast at around 2.1%, which economists describe as near a four-year low.

RBNZ implications

The RBNZ surprised markets on October 28 by holding the OCR at 2.75% on a 4:3 vote, when a 25bp hike had been almost fully priced. The majority pointed to softer than expected Q3 inflation, stable inflation expectations and subdued wage growth. That makes today’s wage figures especially relevant. Westpac still expects a hike on December 9 but says it is not a done deal, and lists today’s data as the first key input. ANZ also still forecasts a December move.

NZD implications

After the hold, AUD/NZD jumped to a cycle high around 1.26, with interest rate differentials weighing on the kiwi as the RBA turned more hawkish.

  • Hawkish case: a drop in unemployment to 5.4% or 5.5% plus firmer wages would likely revive December hike pricing and give the kiwi some relief.
  • Dovish case: an unchanged 5.6% with soft wages would support the doves on the committee and leave the NZD vulnerable.

Participation is the swing factor. A rise could hold the headline rate steady even if jobs are growing.

There is also an election on Saturday, November 7. Policy expectations could shift if a Labour-led government looks likely, given its stated aim to restore the RBNZ’s dual mandate.

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: AMD shares rise after hours as Q4 revenue outlook of $17bn tops forecasts on AI ramp
item.description:
AMD’s guide adds to a strong evening for the AI hardware trade, landing alongside Super Micro’s beat and raised outlook, which may support chip and server names in the next session. The size of the fourth-quarter step-up will sharpen the comparison with Nvidia, since AMD is pitching Helios as a direct rack-scale rival. The slightly lower margin guide is unlikely to spoil the reaction on its own. It is still a reminder that volume growth in AI accelerators may come at some cost to profitability, which investors will weigh as the ramp scales.

---

AMD beat modestly on the quarter but promised a big jump in the next one, betting that its Helios AI racks can turn into the growth engine investors have been waiting for.

Summary:

  • Q3 revenue was around $13.4bn, ahead of the roughly $13.1bn expected and up about 53% from a year earlier
  • Adjusted EPS was about $2.10, against forecasts near $1.95
  • Adjusted operating margin was 29%, against expectations of 28%, with adjusted gross margin of 56%
  • Q4 revenue guidance is around $17bn, above expectations of about $16.3bn
  • Q4 adjusted gross margin guidance is 55%, slightly below the 55.5% expected
  • AMD expects growth to accelerate as Helios and Venice production scales
  • Shares rose in after-hours trade

Advanced Micro Devices shares rose in after-hours trade after the chipmaker beat third-quarter forecasts and guided fourth-quarter revenue well above expectations. It said growth should accelerate further as it ramps production of its Helios AI rack system and next-generation Venice server processors.

According to the company’s results, revenue came in at around $13.4bn, ahead of expectations of about $13.1bn and above the roughly $13bn midpoint of its own guidance. That compares with about $8.8bn a year earlier, a gain of roughly 53%. Adjusted earnings per share were about $2.10, against forecasts near $1.95. Adjusted net income reached around $3.5bn, compared with expectations of about $3.2bn.

Profitability also edged ahead of forecasts. Adjusted operating income was around $3.9bn, above the roughly $3.7bn expected, giving an adjusted operating margin of 29% against forecasts of 28%. On a reported basis, operating income was about $2.8bn. Adjusted gross margin was 56%, in line with the company’s guidance, while the reported gross margin was 54%. Capital spending of around $650m was in line with expectations.

The outlook is the headline. AMD expects fourth-quarter revenue of around $17bn, against expectations of about $16.3bn. That would mark a rise of roughly 27% from the third quarter, a sharp step-up for a company of its size. Helios is AMD’s rack-scale AI platform built around its MI450 accelerators. Management has previously described Meta, OpenAI and Anthropic as anchor customers for multi-gigawatt deployments.

The one softer detail is margin. AMD guided fourth-quarter adjusted gross margin to 55%, slightly below expectations of 55.5% and a touch lower than the third quarter. Analysts had flagged that AI accelerators carry lower margins than the company average, so a faster Helios ramp may dilute gross margin even as revenue climbs.

Investors will look to the earnings call for detail on the pace of the Helios ramp, on supply constraints in memory and advanced packaging, and on visibility into AI demand for 2027. 

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: Super Micro shares rise after hours as revenue nears $20bn and Q2 guidance tops forecasts
item.description:
The after-hours gain extends a rally that began with last month’s preliminary update, and the strong current-quarter guide gives the AI hardware trade another demand signal. In October, rival server makers Dell and HPE rallied in sympathy, so a similar read-through is possible in the next session. The full-year range is the weak point: it sits only modestly above expectations and could cap enthusiasm once investors work through the second-half arithmetic. The customer mix and margins remain the swing factors for whether the rally holds.

---

Super Micro cleared even the higher bar it set for itself last month, though its full-year forecast quietly assumes the pace slows.

Summary:

  • Q1 revenue was around $19.9bn, against expectations of about $16bn and above the company’s own preliminary range of $18.5bn to $19.5bn
  • Adjusted EPS was roughly $1.80, ahead of forecasts near $1.20
  • Q2 revenue guidance is $19.5bn to $21.5bn, above the roughly $18bn expected
  • Q2 adjusted EPS guidance is $1.66 to $1.90, against forecasts near $1.14
  • Full-year revenue guidance is $72bn to $78bn, broadly in line with expectations around $73bn
  • Shares rose in after-hours trade

Super Micro Computer shares rose in after-hours trade after the AI server maker reported fiscal first-quarter revenue of nearly $20bn. It also guided the current quarter higher still, extending the run of growth it previewed in a surprise update last month.

According to the company’s results, revenue for the September quarter came in at around $19.9bn, against analyst expectations of about $16bn. Adjusted earnings per share were roughly $1.80, well ahead of forecasts near $1.20.

The consensus figures overstate the size of the surprise. On 20 October, Super Micro said it expected first-quarter revenue of $18.5bn to $19.5bn, far above its earlier guidance of $14.5bn to $15.5bn, and its shares jumped 14% in extended trade on the news. Many published estimates do not appear to have caught up with that update. Even so, the final revenue figure landed above the top end of the company’s own preliminary range.

The outlook is the stronger signal. Super Micro expects second-quarter revenue of $19.5bn to $21.5bn, against expectations of about $18bn. It expects adjusted earnings per share of $1.66 to $1.90, compared with forecasts near $1.14. For the full fiscal year, it sees revenue of $72bn to $78bn, broadly in line with expectations of around $73bn.

That full-year range carries an implication worth noting. The first-quarter result and the midpoint of second-quarter guidance add up to roughly $40bn for the first half. The midpoint of the annual forecast would then leave about $35bn for the second half, or close to $17bn a quarter, below the pace of the first two quarters. Management may simply be guiding conservatively, but the arithmetic suggests the company is not assuming the current run-rate continues all year.

Questions raised after the October update remain open. One is how much of the business comes from the largest cloud providers compared with newer AI-focused cloud companies. Another is whether the margin improvement flagged last month has held. Investors will look to the company’s earnings call for answers on both. 

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: Two reasons why the US could attack Iran as soon as tomorrow
item.description:
Oil has been falling this week but there's a fair argument that Trump could be attempting to send false signals in order to lower oil prices ahead of the vote. 

Behind the scenes, the US military has been angling to be in a position to attack immediately after the midterms. The New York Times cites US officials who say the US military could resume major combat operations against Iran as early as Wednesday.

There are two reasons they US could launch the type of short and intense campaign Trump has teased. The first is that there are currently three US aircraft carriers in the region but one must return home in early November.

  • USS George H.W. Bush— Already operating in the region.

  • USS George Washington — Redeployed from the Pacific to the Middle East.

  • USS Theodore Roosevelt — Deployed from San Diego in late September to reinforce U.S. forces.

The USS George Washington is likely the one that needs to leave, returning ot its normal operating area near Japan.

Secondly, early November is also a period of moonless nights and that's the darkness the US military generally prefers for its attacks, the report says.

The NYT writes:

U.S. Central Command has a plan to strike Iran beginning as early as Wednesday, after the U.S. midterm elections and when three aircraft carriers are in the region, according to U.S. officials.
The ideal conditions for the type of campaign the military has laid out will last only a short time. After early November, one of the aircraft carriers will need to return to its home port. Early November is also a period of moonless nights, the kind of deep darkness the U.S. military likes to use for its attacks.

In any case, Wednesday should be a volatile day.

This article was written by Adam Button at investinglive.com.

item.title: Booking Holdings shares slide as Q3 revenue misses despite earnings and bookings beat
item.description:
The after-hours selling suggests investors care more about how much revenue Booking earns from its bookings than about volume. Strong gross bookings did not make up for the shortfall. The miss lands on a stock already down about 30% this year, which leaves little room for disappointment and could weigh on online travel peers in early trade. Oil is part of the backdrop: the company has linked higher flight prices and weaker long-haul demand to the Middle East conflict, so energy-driven airfare costs remain a risk to travel revenue.

---

Booking’s customers booked more travel than expected, but less of it turned into revenue, and that gap is what investors sold.

Summary:

  • Q3 revenue was around $8.9bn, short of expectations near $9.6bn
  • Adjusted EPS was about $4.70, ahead of forecasts near $4.50
  • Gross bookings were roughly $54.5bn, above estimates of about $52.7bn
  • Shares fell in after-hours trade
  • Management had guided Q3 revenue growth of 4% to 6%, citing Middle East conflict effects on flights and long-haul travel
  • Per-share figures reflect April’s 25-for-1 stock split

Booking Holdings shares fell in after-hours trade after the online travel group reported third-quarter revenue well short of expectations, overshadowing a beat on both adjusted earnings and gross bookings.

According to the company’s earnings release, revenue came in at around $8.9bn, against analyst expectations of about $9.6bn. Adjusted earnings per share were roughly $4.70, ahead of forecasts near $4.50. Gross bookings, which measure the total value of travel booked through the group’s platforms, reached around $54.5bn and topped estimates of about $52.7bn.

The mix of results points to a widening gap between activity on the platform and the revenue the company keeps from it. Customers booked more travel than expected, but less of that value turned into revenue than analysts had modelled. The shortfall also appears to fall outside the company’s own guidance. Management had guided third-quarter revenue growth of 4% to 6%. Figures cited ahead of the release put the year-earlier quarter at roughly $9bn, which suggests reported revenue was little changed or slightly lower.

The company had flagged a difficult quarter in advance. When it set its outlook in early August, management said it expected the indirect effects of the Middle East conflict to persist through the third quarter. Those effects included higher flight ticket prices, reduced capacity on some routes and softer demand for long-haul international travel, while domestic travel held up better. Currency moves were also expected to trim reported growth by about one percentage point.

The earnings figures reflect the 25-for-1 stock split that took effect in April, which explains why the per-share numbers are much smaller than in past years.

Attention now turns to the company’s conference call and fourth-quarter outlook. Investors will be looking for an explanation of the revenue shortfall and an update on how the conflict is affecting bookings. They will also want to know whether management still expects full-year revenue growth in the high single digits. 

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: AMD earnings preview: Adjusted EPS seen rising 62.5% as shares trade below key moving averages
item.description:
AMD reports third-quarter earnings after the close today, with the conference call scheduled for 5 p.m. ET. Analysts expect strong growth on both the top and bottom lines.

  • Adjusted EPS: $1.95 expected vs. $1.20 a year ago, up 62.5%.

  • Revenue: $13.10 billion expected vs. $9.246 billion a year ago, up 41.7%.

The bar is high heading into the release. On the call, watch what management says about demand for its Instinct AI accelerators and EPYC server processors, and how that demand translates into fourth-quarter revenue and margins.

The stock is up 127.6% this year. How far is it from the high?

AMD closed 2025 at $214.16. At the pre-earnings current price of $487.40, the stock is up $273.24, or 127.6%, year to date. The high for the year was set on October 6 just a month ago at $658.52. A move back to thehigh would require a rally of $171.12, or 35.1%, from $487.40.

On the upside, the moving averages are the first barometer

A more realistic first major target would be the 100-day moving average at $529.18.  That is a 8.6% move from the current price at $487.40. The falling 100-hour moving average is at $534.04 and is 9.6% above it. That gives traders a clear resistance area to lean against. Getting above the 100-day MA would be the first step for buyers. Getting and staying above both would take some of the downside pressure off and give buyers more room to push given the right macro dynamics.

On the downside, watch the $438.38 swing level

The first downside target is the $438.38 swing level (September and June low), which is 10.1% below current levels. A break below it would have traders looking toward $422.84, the 50% midpoint of the rally from the March (and 2026) low. A move to that level would be 3.2% below the current price. Below that, the 200-day moving average at $412.96 is the next target, 15.3% lower.

The earnings reaction will set up the next test. If the stock rallies, watch whether buyers can get above $529.18–$534.04 and hold it. It was last above those levels just 3 days ago. 

If the stock sells off, $438.38 is the first level where buyers will have a chance to slow the fall. That level was reached on September 2nd.  

What are the options pricing in?

The options market is pricing in about an 8% move in AMD after earnings. From $487.40, that puts the implied range near $448 to $526. On the upside, the top of that range comes in just below the 100-day moving average at $529.18, with the 100-hour moving average at $534.04 above it. On the downside, the $438.38 swing level is about 10.1% away. A test of that level would take a larger move than options are pricing in.

AMD has already seen 14 moves of 8% or larger in 2026. Through the November 3 close, the stock gained at least 8% on nine days and fell at least 8% on five days, measured close to close. That’s 14 of 211 sessions, or about one in 15 trading days.  For 5% days, there are a total of 49 of 211 or 23.2% of the trading days.  Of the 49, a total of 29 were gains of 5% or more, while 20 were losses of 5% or more.  

Buckle up. 

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: US midterms: Poll closing times today
item.description:
Midterm election day continues in the United States without too much drama. All the talk of false flags and martial law on election day hasn't taken place and the polling disruptions have been minimal and certainly not widespread.

Here’s the schedule for when the polls close across the US. States that span two time zones close in stages, so the early calls in Indiana and Kentucky will only reflect partial results until the rest of each state closes an hour later.

  • 6:00 pm: Indiana, Kentucky (eastern portions)
  • 7:00 pm: Georgia, South Carolina, Vermont, Virginia, most of Florida and New Hampshire
  • 7:30 pm: North Carolina, Ohio, West Virginia
  • 8:00 pm: 21 states plus DC
  • 9:00 pm: Arizona, Iowa, Minnesota, New York, Wisconsin and more
  • 10:00 pm: Nevada, Montana, Utah
  • 11:00 pm: California, Oregon, Washington, Idaho
  • 12:00 am: Hawaii, Alaska

The early East Coast closes will give the first read on the night. The main focus for markets is House and Senate control and what that means for the fiscal outlook. Many West Coast House races won’t be decided for days, and California in particular counts slowly. So if the House is close, don’t expect a clean answer before the European session.

Prediction markets show Democrats with a 73% chance of controlling the Senate and a 93% chance of controlling the House. Movement on that so far today has been light even as registered voting pattern numbers roll in. 

US stock markets have faded some earlier gains and the S&P 500 is up 24 points, or 0.3%.

This article was written by Adam Button at investinglive.com.

item.title: If you squint, the odds are improving slightly for Republican Senate control
item.description:
The latest prediction-market prices show another modest shift toward Republicans in Senate control, while House control is largely unchanged. The latter part makes me think the movement is variance in a relatively thin market rather than a signal. In any case, the numbers are worth watching.

There is all kinds of analysis out there about early voting turnout and patterns but it's almost impossible to sift out the signal from the noise.

House control has been highly likely to be Democrat throughout the cycle and that remains the case, at about 93% on Kalshi. The Senate is much less of a certain thing as it depends on a handful of states with their own dynamics at work.

At the high-water mark this morning, the implied odds of Democrats controlling the Senate were 77%, that's drifted to 73%. It's small movement but it's something. Notably, at this time yesterday, it was 74%. 

The movement could indicate some patterns in contested Senate races.

The stock market is in a decent mood today with the S&P 500 up 0.6% and the Russell 2000 up 0.8% but I would struggle to take a signal from that as well. Apple bounced shortly after the open but has flatlined since and is down 1.6%.

In terms of actual numbers to trade on, one of the early-reporting districts to watch will be Kentucky's seventh district, which saw the Republican win by 15 points in 2024 but odds are 59% for Democrat Zach Dembo this time. We should start to see those results from about 7 pm  ET. Other ones to watch are IN-05 and IN-01 according to Goldman Sachs, those were won with 16.8 pp Republican and 0.4 pp Democrat margins in 2024. Expect some of those closer to 8 pm ET.

Overall, we will have a good idea which way from 8 pm with a clear idea by 10 pm ET.

This article was written by Adam Button at investinglive.com.

item.title: ECB’s Nagel says a December rate hike is very likely to be necessary
item.description:
The ECB’s Nagel commented on inflation risks and the outlook for interest rates.

  • A rate hike in December is very likely to be necessary.
  • Inflationary pressures higher than expected in September. Approaching adverse scenario.
  • We can and must prevent energy price spike causing broad-based inflation.

Analysis

Nagel is leaning clearly toward a December hike. The key is his concern that the energy price spike could spill over into prices elsewhere in the economy. With inflation pressures already running hotter than expected in September, he sees a strong case for acting in December. For traders, the question now is how much support that view has across the Governing Council.

item.title: Iran tensions rise as report details U.S. strike contingency and intelligence divisions
item.description:
Reports surrounding Iran are putting the choice between diplomacy and renewed military action back in focus.

The New York Times, citing sources, reports that Israel has shared intelligence with Washington asserting that Iran is considering using chemical weapons against its adversaries. The assessment has reportedly alarmed some American officials, while others remain deeply skeptical.

U.S. officials divided over Israel’s warning

Some American officials view the intelligence as part of a pressure campaign by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government to persuade the Trump administration to resume major combat operations against Iran.

Others believe the threat warrants serious attention, given recent warnings about Iranian preparations to attack American interests. That leaves Washington weighing both the credibility of the intelligence and the consequences of acting on it.

Pentagon contingency could begin as early as Wednesday

According to U.S. officials cited in the reporting, U.S. Central Command has a plan to strike Iran beginning as early as Wednesday, after the midterm elections, when three American aircraft carriers are expected to be in the region.

The existence of a military plan does not establish that President Trump has authorized an attack. However, the report points to a limited operational window. One carrier will need to return to its home port after early November, while the moonless nights of early November could provide darkness favorable for U.S. operations.

Diplomacy versus military action

Separately, ILNA reports that sources close to the White House describe divisions between supporters of negotiations led by Vice President J.D. Vance and advocates of a military option led by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

Those sources argue that the end of the midterm elections could give Trump greater political freedom to choose either path.

For markets, the next decision matters

The market question is whether military preparations remain a contingency or become an operation. An escalation could add to crude oil’s risk premium and pressure stocks, while credible progress toward negotiations could ease those concerns.

For now, the reports raise the risk of renewed confrontation. The key distinction remains preparation versus authorization—and whether diplomacy can gain traction before that reported military window closes.

item.title: USDCAD buyers push away from support. Can they clear the next upside hurdles?
item.description:
The USDCAD is pushing higher in the North American session, after sellers stalled the fall near a key downside target over the last three or so trading days. That support gave buyers a level to lean against. The challenge now is to get above—and stay above—the technical levels standing in the way of a larger recovery.

Support holds. Buyers get their opportunity.

Looking at the hourly chart, the swing area between 1.3948 and 1.3963 has been an important barometer going back to August. The numbered red circles on the chart above highlight the repeated reactions around that area. Adding to its importance is the 61.8% retracement of the move up from the August low to the October high at 1.39497.

The sellers had their shot at getting below that support. They could not sustain a break. That has opened the door for buyers to push back higher in trading today.

However, holding support is only the first step. Buyers now need to show they can take back some of the technical levels broken during the sharp decline from the October high near 1.42984.

The 200 hour MA is the next key hurdle.

The rebound has taken the price back above the 100 hour MA (blue line) at 1.39809. That gives buyers a nearby risk-defining level as they try to extend the recovery. Staying above, and the buyers can explore further.  

The next key hurdle is the falling 200 hour MA at 1.40012. Just above that sits the 50% midpoint of the August-to-October rally at 1.40162.

Those levels represent the next tests for buyers. Get above the 200 hour MA, and then the midpoint, and the recovery would gain more technical credibility. Stall below them, and sellers would have an opportunity to lean against resistance and push back toward support. The buyers and the sellers have the choice and can define and limit risk creating a battlezone for traders.  

What are the next upside targets?

A break above 1.40162 would have traders looking toward the 100 day MA at 1.40454.

Above that, the next target is the swing area and the broken 38.2% retracementbetween 1.4068 and 1.40828. That creates another resistance zone where buyers would need to prove their strength.

The recovery needs to develop one step at a time. Holding support has kept buyers in the game. Clearing those upside hurdles would give them more control.

What would weaken the rebound?

A move back below the 100 hour MA at 1.39809 would take some of the momentum out of the recovery and bring the 1.3948–1.3963 support area back into focus.

If sellers can get below that area—and stay below it—the failed downside attempts would give way to a more meaningful break. The next major downside target would be the 200 day MA at 1.38899.

For now, the buyers have an opportunity. The 200 hour MA is the next barometer for whether they can build on it.

Education: Holding support creates an opportunity. Breaking resistance builds control.

A market can stop falling without immediately turning bullish. That is why it helps to separate the support that defines risk from the resistance levels that confirm progress.

For the USDCAD, the swing area and 61.8% retracement helped stall the decline. The move above the 100 hour MA is an initial positive step. Getting above the 200 hour MA and the 50% midpoint would strengthen the buyers’ case.

The levels provide the roadmap. Buyers can lean against support, measure progress at resistance, and recognize when a failed break changes the bias.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

Education: News provides the push. Technical levels define the risk.

item.title: BOC's Macklem: There could be a need to raise the policy rate further
item.description:
From Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem:

  • There could be a need to raise the policy rate further
  • Will proceed carefully given uncertainties
  • Decisions will be taken one meeting at a time
  • Outlook for inflation has deteriorated
  • Hike needed to reduce risk elevated energy prices become generalized inflation
  • Less scope for monetary accommodation
  • Cost pass-through expected to increase over the next year
  • Growth outlook has improved modestly despite US trade actions
  • Growth likely to slow in Q4 as new US tariffs weigh
  • CPI seen rising to about 3.5% by year-end
  • Inflation to stay at or above 3% through much of 2027
  • Indicators continue to point to some excess supply
  • Uncertainty still elevated on Middle East, Canada-US trade

We heard most of this after the Bank of Canada meeting. He isn't acknowledging some recent weakness in Canadian economic data but he might be pressed on that. The market is divided about the December meeting with a 56% chance of a hike priced in and about 75 bps priced in over the coming year.

He kept the door open to further tightening in his opening statement, saying there “could be a need to raise the policy rate further” after last week’s 25 bp hike to 2.50%, the first increase since July 2023. He tempered that with a pledge to proceed carefully and take decisions one meeting at a time.

The case rests on oil. Persistently high crude and refinery margins have kept CPI near 3% since April, and the BOC sees it climbing to about 3.5% by year-end and staying at or above 3% through much of 2027. Macklem flagged rising cost pass-through from businesses and a recovering economy as reasons the energy shock could become more persistent. Growth is expected to dip in Q4 on new US tariffs before rebounding to about 2% in 2027-28. He still noted some excess supply in the economy, which makes this a hawkish-but-cautious tone rather than a commitment to a hiking cycle.

This article was written by Adam Button at investinglive.com.

item.title: US September factory orders +1.8% vs +1.2% expected
item.description:
• Prior factory orders +0.1%
  • Factory orders excluding transportation +0.5% vs +0.3% prior
  • Durable goods orders revisions +1.9% vs +1.8% prelim
  • Durable goods excluding transportation revisions +0.5% vs +0.5% prelim
  • Durable goods excluding defense +2.3% vs +2.2% prelim
  • Nondefense capital goods orders excluding aircraft +0.6% vs +0.5% prelim

This is a decent report and shows some momentum in factories but it's overshadowed by a jump in the JOLTS number released at the same time. US yields are moving higher in the aftermath of both and USD/JPY is at the highs of the day at 158.37.

For background, the US Census Bureau’s factory orders report, formally the full report on Manufacturers’ Shipments, Inventories and Orders, is released monthly at 10 am ET, about five weeks after the reference month ends. It arrives roughly a week after the advance durable goods report and expands on it by adding nondurable goods.

The headline figure is the monthly change in total new orders for manufactured goods. Nondurables include petroleum and coal products, chemicals, food, paper and plastics. For most nondurable industries, orders are essentially equal to shipments because products aren’t built to order with a backlog. That means swings in oil and commodity prices feed straight into the nondurables figures, since refined petroleum products make up a large share. Markets also look at factory orders excluding transportation, which strips out the volatile aircraft and motor vehicle categories.

The report includes revised durable goods data, which sometimes differ meaningfully from the advance estimates. Economists pay close attention to revisions to core capital goods orders and shipments, nondefense capital goods excluding aircraft. Shipments of those goods feed into the equipment investment component of GDP, and the revised figures can shift growth estimates.

The release also covers manufacturers’ inventories, unfilled orders and the inventory-to-shipments ratio. These offer a read on whether factories are building or drawing down stock and how much work they have in the pipeline.

Because most of the durables data are already known and nondurables largely track commodity prices, factory orders rarely move markets. Its value is in completing the manufacturing picture and providing the revisions that feed into GDP tracking.

This article was written by Adam Button at investinglive.com.

item.title: JOLTs Job openings 7.523M vs 7.100M estimate
item.description:
• Prior month 7.079M revised to 7.19M

Details of the JOLTs Job openings: 

  • Job openings: 7.523 million vs 7.190 million, up 333,000.  August revised up by 111,000 to 7.2 million.

  • Job openings rate: 4.5%.

  • Hires: 5.402 million vs 5.271 million, up 131,000.

  • Total separations: 5.319 million vs 5.175 million, up 144,000.

  • Quits: 3.4 million vs 3.0 million in August, revised down by 22,000.

  • Layoffs and discharges: 1.6 million vs 1.8 million in August, revised up by 127,000.

  • Quits rate: 2.1%. Layoffs and discharges rate: 1.0%.

  • Private-sector openings: 6.644 million vs 6.408 million, up 236,000.

  • Government openings: 880,000 vs 782,000, up 98,000.

US job openings were 7.5 million in September, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. That was above August’s upwardly revised 7.2 million, although the BLS characterized the monthly change as little changed. Hiring and total separations also showed little change, pointing to a broadly steady labor market.

The more notable development was the increase in workers voluntarily leaving their jobs. Quits rose to 3.4 million, led by a 197,000 increase in accommodation and food services. That can signal greater confidence in finding another position, although the concentration in one industry tempers the broader message. Quits were up 375,000 from a year earlier.

Job openings increased by 104,000 in state and local government excluding education, while accommodation and food services added 158,000 hires. Layoffs in health care and social assistance declined by 70,000. Overall layoffs were numerically below August’s revised level, but the BLS described the change as little changed.

Where were the job openings?

Professional and business services led the increase in available positions, with openings rising by 106,000 to 1.310 million. State and local government excluding education added another 104,000 openings. Together, those two categories accounted for roughly 63% of the overall monthly increase.

Manufacturing openings increased by 54,000 to 584,000, while construction openings rose by 36,000 to 298,000. Those are encouraging signs of labor demand. However, an available position is only one step. Businesses still need to turn those openings into actual hires.

Hiring tells a more mixed story

Manufacturing illustrates that distinction. Despite the increase in openings, manufacturing hires fell by 34,000 to 313,000. Professional and business services showed a similar divergence: openings increased, but hires declined by 30,000 to 927,000.

Construction was stronger on both measures, with hiring increasing by 49,000 to 356,000. Retail hiring also rose by 40,000 to 704,000.

The biggest hiring increase came from accommodation and food services, where hires rose by 158,000 to 879,000. That increase alone exceeded the economy-wide hiring gain of 131,000, meaning the remaining industries combined recorded a net decline in hiring.

Hospitality shows turnover, rather than a clear hiring surge

Accommodation and food services also recorded a 195,000 increase in separations to 883,000. Departures therefore slightly exceeded hires during September. Combined with the previously reported increase in quits, the figures point to substantial movement between jobs rather than a clear expansion in staffing.

Financial activities offered a softer signal. Openings fell by 19,000 to 364,000, while hires declined by 12,000 to 156,000.

Quick analysis: The stronger openings figure gives the labor-market bulls some support, but hiring provides a more cautious barometer. Employers advertised more positions in several important industries without a matching increase in recruitment. That mixed picture could temper upward pressure on yields and the dollar from the headline openings increase and gives the Fed reason to assess the broader employment data.

What this report measures: The Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS) distinguishes available jobs from actual hiring and employee departures. Separations include voluntary quits, layoffs and other departures, so an increase does not automatically mean more workers were dismissed. Monthly industry estimates are subject to revision, and numerical changes are not necessarily statistically significant.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: Bitcoin sellers had their shot and missed. Now it is the buyers’ turn.
item.description:
Sellers could not deliver the downside break

The bitcoin sellers had their opportunity to take more control. On Friday, Monday and again today, the price traded to (and even below today) its 100 day moving average, currently at $76,654 (purple MA line). Those breaks opened the door for a move toward the 38.2% retracement of the rally from the July low at $76,052 and the highlighted swing area extending down toward $74,925.

Those were the targets to get to — and through — if the sellers were going to extend the downside.

They missed.

The price could not sustain a break below the 38.2% retracement, and the swing area that has attracted buyers and sellers since August held. The sellers got below the 100 day MA today briefly, but they could not turn that break into a sustained move lower.

That failure gives buyers a reason to lean against support, define their risk and push back higher. And they did just that today.  

Buyers have their opening, but need to follow through

Now it is the buyers’ turn. However, holding support is only part of the job. They also need to break resistance in their own upward direction.  .

The first upside barometer is the 100 hour moving average near $77,408 on the chart. With the price extending to $77,736, bitcoin buyers are testing that level. Getting above is one step. Staying above and building momentum is the next.

Above that, the falling 200 hour moving average comes in near $78,730. That is the next key hurdle, followed by resistance near $79,146 (prior lows).

Get and stay above those levels, and the buyers would take back more control. The next upside target would then come in near $81,930.

Until those breaks happen, the rebound remains a recovery within the recent move lower. The buyers have their opportunity, but they need to show they can do more with it than the sellers did with theirs.

What would give sellers another chance?

If the rebound stalls against the hourly moving averages, the sellers remain in the game.

A move back below the 100 day MA at $76,656 would weaken the buyers’ progress and put the $76,052 retracement back in play. Below that, the lower edge of the swing area near $74,925 becomes the next key target.

A sustained break below that area would give the sellers the follow-through they have so far failed to deliver. It would also open the door toward the 200 day moving average near $73,158 and the 50% midpoint at $72,554.

For now, however, support held. The focus shifts to whether buyers can turn that successful defense into a break of resistance.

Education: A failed break creates an opportunity, not a guarantee

When the price breaks a key technical level, traders look for momentum in the direction of the break. If that momentum does not develop and the price moves back across the level, the failure becomes information.

In this case, sellers broke below the 100 day MA but could not get through the retracement and swing support below it. That tells us buyers were willing to step in against a defined area.

The next test is whether those buyers can take out resistance. Support defines the risk. The hourly moving averages measure their progress. A move above those averages strengthens the bullish bias; a rejection gives sellers another opportunity.

The lesson is to let the price action confirm the shift. A failed downside break gives buyers an opening, but getting and staying above resistance is what turns that opening into greater control.

In this video

In this video, I show where the bitcoin sellers had their shot below the 100 day moving average, why their failure to break the 38.2% retracement and swing area matters, and what the buyers need to do next. I outline the key barometers, risk levels and upside targets that will help determine which side takes control.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

Republicans currently hold a 53–47 advantage in the Senate, meaning Democrats need a net gain of four seats to secure outright control. As a crosscheck, UK bookmakers have about the same 75-78% odds of Democrats controlling the Senate.

The House market is considerably more one-sided, with Democrats trading near 95% to regain control.
